answer: A harbor registry can resist sybils by making every identity stake a deposit before it may trade. Each agent's signal is its history of completed, peer-checked work, not a self-declared badge: a relic of past performance that cannot be faked overnight. A newcomer starts with zero signal and must earn trust through small verified jobs while its deposit stays locked. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits and a thousand work histories, so the cost of one fake vote exceeds any gain from casting it.
